correctness.rationale: Invariant affine hyperplane measure restricted to those intersecting a simplex gives normal density proportional to width and conditional offset Lebesgue uniform. The k-th offset interval is the gap of consecutive vertex projections, so P(K=k) is ratio of expected gaps to expected range. Projecting standard Gaussians onto the zero-sum subspace gives direction independent of radius and the same ratio of ordinary Gaussian spacings. Integrating the event #{G_i<=s}=k gives binomial integral. Each crossed simplex edge yields a section vertex, giving K(N-K); the barycentric rescaling preserves the entire face lattice of Δ_(K-1)×Δ_(N-K-1). Summation of pairwise Gaussian absolute differences gives E V=N(N-1)/(sqrt(pi) M_N). Gaussian maxima M_N~2sqrt(2log N), and the width-normalized auxiliary Gaussian level S/sqrt(2log N) tends to Uniform[-1,1]. For each compact interior level z the smaller binomial count has log exponent 1-z² by Mills and Chernoff bounds; boundaries have vanishing probability. Thus log V/log N ⇒2-U², and V/E V→0 since the limit has no mass at exponent 2.
